# i-have-adhd: output shaped for ADHD readers

Curated by Skill Harbor — @ayghri's session-persistent output style that reshapes every agent answer so an ADHD reader can act on it: lead with the one next action (not context), number multi-step work in single bounded steps, end with one concrete under-two-minutes action, suppress tangents, restate state every turn ("Step 3 of 5 done: schema updated"), give specific time estimates ("about 15 minutes if tests already cover this"), make wins visible in concrete terms, use a matter-of-fact error tone (cause and fix, never "Uh oh"), cap lists at five, and strip preamble, recaps and closing pleasantries — with when-to-break-the-rules overrides (explain requests, destructive actions, debug spirals, real ambiguity, a rule that would delete the answer itself) and a pre-send checklist that deletes announcement sentences, "anything else?" closers, hedges and idioms, ending on a first-line/last-line test: does the reader know what to do next and what just happened? Invoke with /i-have-adhd; it stays on until "stop adhd mode". Honest caveats: it shapes presentation only and never limits the analysis itself; MIT-licensed. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Discovered via skills.sh.
